summary: Case study of a residential mortgage refinance on a property held in a British Virgin Islands (BVI) trust. Deal: a UK landlord had built a large five-bedroom house on a plot in Richmond, South West London, and wanted to replace an expensive development loan with a cheaper residential mortgage. Loan required: GBP 5 million; property valued at GBP 12 million (implied LTV approx. 41.7%, derived, not stated). Structure sought: interest-only facility over 10 years. Rate listed in the terms: 2.7%. Borrower type: UK landlord whose income came from a farming business and a property portfolio, with the property held in an offshore (BVI) trust administered with trustees based in Guernsey. Lender type: a private bank that had a BVI office where the trust was administered. Challenges: (1) finding a lender that would accept the mixed farming/property-portfolio income; (2) the lender needed a working relationship with the Guernsey-based trustees because the property sat in an offshore trust. Outcome: Silver Oak connected the client with the private bank; the listed terms show a GBP 5 million residential mortgage at 2.7%. Timing/completion date: not revealed. Only the opening portion of the page was returned by search; the full write-up may contain more detail.
